summary: Slovenia’s country-specific LULUCF target under the EU framework is -212 Kt CO2eq for 2030. The wider EU framework sets a land-sector sink of -310 Mt CO2-eq by 2030—an increase in net removals of 42 Mt CO2-eq relative to the 2016–2018 average—and calls for restoration measures on at least 20% of EU land and sea areas by 2030, with measures for all ecosystems needing restoration by 2050. EU agricultural provisions allocate 40% of CAP funding to climate objectives in 2023–2027, earmark at least 25% of annual Pillar I direct payments for eco-schemes and 35% of Pillar II funds for environmental and climate activities, and target a 40% cut in non-ETS emissions by 2030 versus 2005. Slovenia is 66.3% forest (13,435 km²) and 28.2% agriculture (5,717 km²), but the restoration and funding percentages are EU-wide, not Slovenian land-area or farm-area shares.
